solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: This writer in Somerset town in a trance?

indicators.note: the writer is placed in the middle of the town's name, so 'in' signals insertion

parts.note: Chard is a small town in Somerset, a county in south-west England
the setter referring to themself gives ME

explanation.surface: A writer drifting about a sleepy West Country town in a dreamy daze.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR + ME + D. The question mark flags that 'in a trance' is a loose, playful definition of being spellbound.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under a spell is held as if hypnotised, which is a trance-like state.

clue.text: Peasant in bed with sailor

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A peasant in bed with a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottar was a Scottish farm labourer living in a cottage, a peasant.

clue.text: One on raft floating around much of day

indicators.note: floating around suggests drifting loosely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone drifting about on a raft for most of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours from noon to evening make up a large portion of the day.

clue.text: Most gentle maiden that is hugging disheartened lad on street

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: hugging means the that-is letters wrap round the cut lad

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: disheartened means the centre letter is removed from lad

explanation.surface: The gentlest maiden hugs a downhearted lad in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild means gentle, and this is its superlative form.

clue.text: Waste in East Anglian town I disposed of, having secured parking

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, in East Anglia, eastern England

indicators.note: having secured means the letters hold the parking abbreviation inside

parts.note: food you have eaten is disposed of, so ate

explanation.surface: Someone frittering money in a Norfolk town after finally finding a parking spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander resources is to waste them.

clue.text: Relief when river is kept outside shelter

indicators.note: the river's letters stay on the outside, wrapping round the shelter

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a tent is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: Relief when a river stays outside your tent rather than flooding in.
explanation.definitionFit: A thaw in hostility between nations brings easing of tension, a kind of relief.

clue.text: Greek detectives turning up to apprehend men

indicators.note: apprehend means catch hold of, so the turned letters enclose the men
in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Detectives show up to arrest some Greek men.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads upwards; 'to apprehend' then makes the reversed detectives grab the men.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doric order and dialect are Greek in origin, so the adjective means Greek.

clue.text: Dramatic scene in which gold is hidden under item of furniture

indicators.note: in a down clue the gold sits below the furniture, after it

parts.note: a table is an item of furniture
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A dramatic scene in which gold is stashed under a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene, often a staged group of motionless figures.

clue.text: Half-hearted dope is good

indicators.note: half-hearted means one of the two central letters is removed

parts.note: to nobble a racehorse is to drug it

explanation.surface: A half-hearted fool is nonetheless good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like a noun for a fool, but it is the verb, to drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble describes fine, virtuous character, so it means good.

clue.text: Fast faller sung of at Cup Final

definitions.text: Fast faller sung of at Cup Final

parts.words: Fast faller sung of at Cup Final
parts.note: the hymn Abide with Me, sung before the FA Cup Final, opens with the line about evening falling fast

explanation.surface: A speedy footballer who falls over is serenaded at the Cup Final.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA Cup Final is English football's showpiece match, where the crowd traditionally sings the hymn Abide with Me.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old poetic term for the evening, the time of day that falls fast in the hymn.

clue.text: Device for gambling? Youngster needs short warning, is enthralled

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: enthralled means captivated, so the cut warning holds the word is captive inside it
short means the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: an alert is a warning

explanation.surface: A gambling machine needs a quick warning because a child is captivated by it.
explanation.definitionFit: A totaliser (the tote) is a machine that pools and records bets at racecourses.

clue.text: Irritability about book in religious literary collection

indicators.note: about means round, so the irritability word goes around the book abbreviation

parts.note: bile is bad temper or irritability

explanation.surface: Getting cross about a book in a collection of religious writings.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripture is a collection of many books of religious writing gathered in one volume.

clue.text: A feature of golf — uncompleted match

indicators.note: uncompleted means the last letter is left off the golf feature

parts.note: a green is the putting area on a golf course

explanation.surface: A golf feature, plus a match left unfinished on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a golf match, but it is the verb meaning correspond.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that match correspond with each other, so they concur.

clue.text: Bitter gain with Left ousting Right

indicators.note: ousting means the left letter takes the place of the right letter

parts.note: an increment is a gain or increase

explanation.surface: A political observation about the Left's bitter gain at the Right's expense.
explanation.walkthrough: In INCREMENT the R is swapped for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter weather is harsh and cold, which is what inclement describes.

clue.text: Ridiculous overdue amount must be circumvented

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests something absurdly jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ridiculous overdue bill must be dodged somehow.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit or outflank an opponent is to get round them, to circumvent them.

clue.text: Cats tormented relations

indicators.note: tormented means twisted and troubled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cats tormenting one's relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Orientals are a group of slender cat breeds related to the Siamese.

clue.text: What author wants — connections to the top people?

parts.note: royal describes the people at the very top of society, kings and queens
ties are connections or links

explanation.surface: A writer hoping for income, or for links to the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers are paid a percentage of the sales of each copy, which is what they hope to earn.

clue.text: Forceful English politician in charge should admit pork pie maybe

indicators.note: admit means let in, so these letters take the pie hat inside

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
a pork pie is a flat-crowned style of hat

explanation.surface: An English politician in charge ought to own up to eating a pork pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pie' looks like food but here is the round flat-topped hat.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic statement is made with force and conviction.

clue.text: Little Sarah embraces new rite as a clergywoman?

parts.note: mini means little

indicators.note: embraces means the name holds the shuffled letters inside it

parts.note: Sally is a pet form of the name Sarah

indicators.note: new means the letters of rite are made into a new order

explanation.surface: Little Sarah takes up a new rite, as if she were a clergywoman.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled rite sits just after the first letter of the pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergywoman acts in the role of a minister of religion, hence in a ministerial way.

clue.text: Frighten in heartless manner with cunning intervention

indicators.note: intervention means coming in between, so the cunning word goes inside
heartless means the central letter is removed

parts.note: style means manner
art can mean cunning or craft

explanation.surface: Scaring someone with a heartless approach and some sly meddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' cuts STYLE to STLE; 'intervention' puts ART into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a sudden shock or fright is to make them jump.

clue.text: Make fun of a fairly quiet twerp going round

indicators.note: going round means the twerp word encircles the other letters

parts.note: a loon is a silly or foolish person
mp, mezzo piano, is the musical marking for moderately soft

explanation.surface: Mocking a rather quiet fool who is wandering about.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise someone is to mock or ridicule them.

clue.text: Big inmate finally escapes and is free

indicators.note: escapes means that letter leaves the big word

parts.note: great means big

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of inmate

explanation.surface: A hulking prisoner finally breaks out and is free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like at liberty, but here means without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given for nothing costs nothing, so it is without charge.

clue.text: European suspended, one deemed heretical

parts.note: hung means suspended
an Arian followed Arius, whose teaching on the Trinity was condemned as heresy

explanation.surface: A European left hanging after being judged a heretic.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Hungary, a central European country, is a European.

clue.text: Currently at the crease and hopeless?

parts.note: now means currently
a batter at the crease in cricket is in

explanation.surface: A batter now at the crease with no hope of success.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the batting line; a batter there is IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation one cannot succeed in, whatever one does, is without hope.

clue.text: Hint in straightforward manner: Leader must go

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: simply means in a plain, straightforward way

explanation.surface: A blunt hint: the leader must resign.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest without saying outright is to hint.

clue.text: Sender of message dispatching a runner

indicators.note: dispatching means getting rid of, so the letter a is removed

parts.note: a mailer is one who sends mail

explanation.surface: Someone sending a message by dispatching a runner, a messenger on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who specialises in the one-mile race is named after that distance.

clue.text: Child impeded by group of women, as you would say?

indicators.note: impeded by means the child is blocked in the middle by the group

parts.note: a tot is a small child
WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation

explanation.surface: A child held up by a group of women, as you might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British community organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a restatement, meaning namely or that is to say.

clue.text: The French fashion is in part one promoting particular philosophy

indicators.note: in means the run of letters is placed inside the part abbreviation

parts.note: la is French for the
ton means fashion or style

explanation.surface: French fashion features in part of an argument for a particular philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Plato advocates his particular school of thought.

clue.text: Show emotion when old queen enters factory

indicators.note: enters means the queen goes inside the emotion word

parts.note: to cry is to show emotion
Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: Workers show emotion when an old queen comes into the factory on a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant where food is sealed in tins is a type of factory.

clue.text: Evil exercises? They can give you a headache

definitions.text: They can give you a headache

parts.note: sin is evil
to exercise a right is to use it, so exercises means uses

explanation.surface: Wicked workouts: they can leave you with a headache.
explanation.definitionFit: Blocked or inflamed cavities in the skull behind the face cause headaches.
